::: {#exm-broadcasting}

#### Broadcasting the average image

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
print(torch.broadcast_shapes(images.shape, mean_image.shape))
print(torch.broadcast_shapes(images.shape, mean_image[0].shape))
print(torch.broadcast_shapes(images.shape, (len(images), 1, 1)))
```

In @sol-center-images, the [shapes](#def-shape) (`r py$n_images`, 8, 8) and (8, 8) line up as 8 with 8, 8 with 8,
and `r py$n_images` with a missing dimension, which counts as 1,
so the result has [shape](#def-shape) (`r py$n_images`, 8, 8).
A single row of the average image, of shape (8,), is also compatible:
it is used for every row of every image.
So is a shape of (`r py$n_images`, 1, 1), one number per image,
which is used for every pixel of its image.
`torch.broadcast_shapes` applies the rule to shapes alone, without any data.

:::
